assertions.text: Review names Cynefin domain as Complex (or notes multiple emergent dimensions)
assertions.evidence: Section 7: 'The problem space is "complex," not "complicated"' and 'cause-and-effect is genuinely emergent'

assertions.text: Review selects Full tier (quarter-long appetite, multiple themes)
assertions.evidence: No explicit tier naming (Fast-track / Standard / Full) anywhere in the review.

assertions.text: B1 (problem framing) verdict is SUSTAINED or PARTIAL — themes named without measurable outcomes
assertions.evidence: Section 1: 'Themes are framed as solutions, not problems'; Section 2: 'No measurable success criteria... None of the three themes has a target metric.'

assertions.text: B2 (scope) verdict is SUSTAINED — at least one theme has scope-vague concern (no triage record cited)
assertions.evidence: Section 4: 'No triage / discovery work named'; 'A rewrite is an enormous appetite for an undiagnosed issue.'

assertions.text: B3 (assumptions) verdict is SUSTAINED — at least one assumption flagged as low-confidence/anecdotal
assertions.evidence: Section 3: 'Shareable shortlist — confidence ~0.5. "We keep getting requests" is anecdotal.'

assertions.text: B3 includes a numeric confidence score (Gilad Confidence Meter, 0.1–10) on at least one assumption
assertions.evidence: Section 3: 'Using a rough confidence scale (Gilad-style, 0.1 = opinion, 0.5 = anecdotal, 2-3 = survey/analytics, 5+ = experimental evidence)' with explicit ~0.5 scores assigned.

assertions.text: Review recommends running idea-triage on themes before allocation
assertions.evidence: Line 79: 'Run formal triage on the three themes (problem framing, ICE/confidence scoring, kill criteria).'

assertions.text: At least one bucket has a named falsifying condition (concrete check that would overturn the verdict)
assertions.evidence: Explicit 'Falsifying conditions' section: 'Shortlist: you have a written tally of >50 distinct requests, segmented, showing the same underlying job-to-be-done...'
